_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary head term for the site's core copy-paste font tool. Already the site's #1 BR term — keep it undiluted, do not stuff synonyms around it.
phrases.good_example: Letras diferentes para copiar e colar
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — this is the safe default term

phrases.usage_guidance: Safe supporting descriptor, pairs naturally with 'letras diferentes.' Don't over-rely on it as a standalone H1 term — competitors already saturate it (fonteparaig.com claims '+1000 Letras Bonitas').
phrases.good_example: Gerador de fontes online: letras diferentes, fontes bonitas e símbolos aesthetic
phrases.avoid_when: aggressive/dark gamer-name contexts (use 'estiloso'/'sombrio' instead)

phrases.usage_guidance: Preferred over 'bonito' in gaming/nick contexts — carries a slightly more masculine/neutral gamer register than 'bonito/fofo'.
phrases.good_example: Crie seu nick FF com símbolos... e letras diferentes. [...] nick estiloso
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: copiar e colar / copia e cola
phrases.register: neutral (copiar e colar) vs. informal/branded (copia e cola)
phrases.content_surface: title, meta, button labels, FAQ answers throughout
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the infinitive 'copiar e colar' in titles/meta (formal-neutral, matches how Google users phrase the query); the imperative 'copie e cole' is fine in FAQ body copy; 'copia e cola' (no accent/present-indicative) is a valid informal brand-name-style variant seen on competitor titles but reads slightly more casual/click-baity.
phrases.good_example: Digite seu texto [...] Clica em «Copiar» [...] e cola onde quiser
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.register: informal/colloquial (diminutive) — this is the user-voice term, vs. the more editorial 'quadrado'
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the diminutive 'quadradinho' in user-facing troubleshooting copy (it's the actual word players use — one fetched source puts it in scare quotes precisely because it's quoting user slang); 'quadrado' is fine in more neutral/editorial explainer prose.
phrases.good_example: Por que meu nick aparece como quadradinho (▯)?
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary term for this feature. Specify both real fallback characters found live in the repo and in the wild: Hangul filler U+3164 (ㅤ) as the dominant/large option, Braille blank U+2800 (⠀) as the alternate/safer option. Frame the job explicitly as 'to separate symbols from the name' — that's the actual stated use case, not 'to make a blank name.'
phrases.good_example: O Free Fire não aceita o espaço comum no nick. O truque é usar um caractere invisível: o caractere de preenchimento Hangul (ㅤ, U+3164)
phrases.avoid_when: 'nome em branco' — this specific phrasing did not surface in dedicated forum research; the real BR framing centers on spacing/separation, not a fully blank name

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the umbrella/reference term (vs. 'espaço invisível' which is the task-specific variant). Both are natural BR phrasing and coexist correctly across three distinct live PT pages.
phrases.good_example: Caractere Invisível (⠀): Nomes em Branco, Significado e Como Usar
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: H1, titles throughout gaming usecase pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Dominant term in gaming contexts — use 'nick' not 'apelido' for game-name pages. Note the register split: Garena's own official support docs use 'apelido'/'Nickname' interchangeably (formal/support register), while player-facing/community copy overwhelmingly says 'nick.' A real BR user was observed code-switching nick→apelido within the same sentence on Steam, so both are understood, but 'nick' is the on-brand choice for tool UI.
phrases.good_example: Gerador de nick FF — nomes e símbolos para Free Fire
phrases.avoid_when: formal/official support-style copy (use 'apelido' there instead, matching Garena's own register)

phrases.usage_guidance: Use where a more formal/official register fits (guides, official-sounding explainers), or when writing content that pairs with a platform's own official terminology (Garena's support docs use this word).
phrases.good_example: Evite a utilização de caracteres especiais ao escolher o novo nickname [Garena official, mixes 'nickname' and 'apelido']
phrases.avoid_when: casual gamer-facing UI copy (prefer 'nick')

phrases.content_surface: usecase page title, hero, FAQ throughout
phrases.usage_guidance: Use untranslated 'bio' — this is not a translation gap, it's the actual BR word (no one says 'descrição de perfil' colloquially). Reserve 'descrição de perfil' for more formal/technical explainer sentences alongside it.
phrases.good_example: Bio bonita pro Insta
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: nome de guilda / tag de guilda
phrases.english_concept: Free Fire guild name / clan tag generator
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary shipped term, already performing in GSC (per an internal GSC query pull) — keep as-is.
phrases.good_example: Nomes para Guilda Free Fire — Gerador de Tag de Squad
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: nome de clã / tag de clã
phrases.english_concept: clan tag (colloquial manual-convention term, distinct from official guild name)
phrases.register: informal, used interchangeably with 'guilda' in fan content
phrases.content_surface: JSON-LD alternateName only (not visible body copy)
phrases.usage_guidance: Real, well-evidenced BR term — safe to surface in visible copy (H2/FAQ), not just schema metadata. Also seen as 'Times'/'Lines' in one BR source (mobilegamer.com.br) as sibling group-name vocabulary worth testing.
phrases.good_example: Free Fire: 1.300 Nomes de Guilda (Clã, Times, Lines)
phrases.avoid_when: implying Free Fire has an official separate clan-tag field — it does not; frame as a player convention, same nuance internal clan/guild-tag research already flagged

phrases.native_phrase: Display Name vs. nome de usuário
phrases.english_concept: Roblox's two separate name fields (login username vs. cosmetic display name)
phrases.register: neutral, mixes untranslated English UI term with Portuguese
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep 'Display Name' untranslated (it's the literal UI label Roblox itself shows in PT locales) paired with 'nome de usuário' for the login field — this mirrors game-rules.js's own roblox/robloxDisplay split (username: asciiPattern-locked, limit 20; display: no ascii lock, limit 20).
phrases.good_example: n/a (dictionary-carried; confirm current on-page wording against /pt/library/simbolos-roblox/ and /pt/usecase/nomes-para-roblox/ before quoting verbatim)
phrases.avoid_when: implying symbols work in the login username field — they do not

phrases.content_surface: not currently used on the PT site
phrases.usage_guidance: Candidate for informal BR copy (social captions, casual FAQ tone) but not yet used anywhere on the PT site — 'estiloso'/'legal'/'bonito' currently cover this ground. Test in a low-stakes surface (e.g. a casual FAQ answer or social caption example) before committing to headline copy.
phrases.good_example: n/a — no on-topic (text-styling) BR source found this pass; this is general-register slang confirmation only
phrases.avoid_when: formal/official-sounding copy (meta descriptions, JSON-LD)

phrases.content_surface: not on the pt_BR-tuned site (correctly so — do not force into BR copy)
phrases.usage_guidance: Reserve strictly for a future dedicated pt_PT variant, never mix into the pt_BR-primary site. 'fixe' ≈ 'legal/bacana/maneiro'; 'giro/gira' ≈ 'bonito/bom.' Do not assume a query like 'letra gira' has real search volume without a dedicated pt_PT validation pass — no text-styling-context usage was found, only general slang-dictionary confirmation.
phrases.good_example: n/a — no text-styling-context BR/PT source found; slang-dictionary confirmation only
phrases.avoid_when: any pt_BR-primary page — this is a market-specific register, not a synonym to sprinkle into BR copy

phrases.content_surface: not currently addressed anywhere on the PT site
phrases.usage_guidance: Real, well-evidenced BR metaphor for excessive decoration — 'poluído' (polluted) is the native opposite pole of 'elegante.' Strong candidate for a UI warning/tip ('não exagere' style nudge) on any symbol-heavy generator page (nick-ff, guilda), which currently has no such guidance despite shipping 'Combinações Raras' encouraging MORE symbol stacking.
phrases.good_example: um nick elegante e um poluído [...] exagerar na quantidade de símbolos, criando um nome ilegível
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: saia do básico / se destacar / único
phrases.content_surface: not currently used verbatim on the PT site (site uses 'diferentona'/'diferentes' framing instead)
phrases.usage_guidance: 'destacar' is the recurring verb across independent BR sources for this concept — stronger and more idiomatic than a literal 'único' alone. Good candidate phrase for a 'Combinações Raras' style section's intro copy.
phrases.good_example: 47 ideias de símbolos para nick: saia do básico e seja único
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: not currently used on ultratextgen.com's own PT copy (external gaming-content usage only) — the feminine 'diferentona' previously cited here as this phrase's own existing usage is now tracked separately as PT-063, since research found the two forms carry different connotations.
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the attested plural masculine form 'diferentões' (or singular 'diferentão') for neutral-positive 'strikingly unique/different' framing in gamer-nickname contexts — directly evidenced 2026-08-04 (Pichau Arena). Do NOT treat the feminine 'diferentona' as an interchangeable variant — see PT-063: it carries documented ironic/meme connotations this masculine form does not.
phrases.good_example: "Konoha_Child" ou "Raikage_Man" podem ser Nicks mais acessíveis e diferentões para usar nas partidas — Pichau Arena Free Fire nickname guide (2023-08-11), directly fetched 2026-08-04.
phrases.avoid_when: meta descriptions/titles (too informal, unverified at scale)

phrases.usage_guidance: Existing, natural, already-shipped category framing — keep. Note the underlying naming pattern is noun-based (Death, Reaper, Wraith, Necro / Savage, Predator, Warlord, Venom, Ragnarok), matching independently-observed BR community convention of naming via dark/power nouns rather than adjectives.
phrases.good_example: ꧁☬ᴅᴇᴀᴛʜ☬꧂ / ༺†ᴄᴜʀsᴇ†༻ / ⚰𝔇𝔢𝔪𝔬𝔫⚰ [live examples from the shipped page]
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: cara do Brasil / Tags de Guilda Brasileiras
phrases.usage_guidance: Existing, natural, on-brand local-flavor framing — keep. Examples used (Fúria, Tropa, Brasen, Elite, Nova, Ace) lean esports-team-name register rather than generic Brazilian cultural symbols, which fits the Free Fire competitive audience.
phrases.good_example: Curtas, com a cara do Brasil — fáceis de encaixar num time inteiro.
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: not currently a dedicated concept on the PT site
phrases.usage_guidance: Official term used by both Discord's own PT-BR support docs (for its Nitro-gated 'Estilos de nome exibido' feature) and general BR editorial content for WhatsApp's status/display-name field. Strong candidate for a 'free alternative to Discord Nitro name styling' framing already flagged in prior JTBD research.
phrases.good_example: FAQ sobre os Estilos de nome exibido do Discord [Discord's own PT-BR support article title]
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: FAQ section headers, library collection pages
phrases.usage_guidance: BR does NOT translate these labels — it loans the English/Japanese aesthetic word directly and pairs it with a Portuguese modifier where needed (e.g. 'Feminino Delicado' alongside untranslated 'Soft Aesthetic', 'Dark Aesthetic'). This matches the site's own existing practice exactly — keep doing this, don't force translations like 'estética suave'.
phrases.good_example: Onde acho símbolos aesthetic, coquette e bonitos pra copiar?
phrases.avoid_when: forcing a literal Portuguese translation of 'aesthetic'/'coquette'/'kawaii'/'y2k' themselves — that would be unnatural

phrases.content_surface: not the site's primary term (site prefers 'símbolos') but a natural synonym
phrases.usage_guidance: Use interchangeably with 'símbolos' in explainer/definitional sentences; 'símbolos' remains the better UI/button-label word (shorter, more casual).
phrases.good_example: Caracteres especiais são símbolos que vão além das letras e números do teclado convencional [...] Todos fazem parte do padrão Unicode
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: not currently addressed on the PT site
phrases.usage_guidance: Frame rejection as Garena's own official hedge, not an absolute ban: their support doc does NOT say symbols are banned, it says results aren't guaranteed. This is a more accurate, more trustworthy framing than a flat 'X symbols will get you banned/rejected' claim.
phrases.good_example: Evite a utilização de caracteres especiais ao escolher o novo nickname. Não podemos garantir que todos eles apareçam. [Garena official, fetched]
phrases.avoid_when: overstating rejection as a hard technical ban rather than a rendering/moderation risk

phrases.english_concept: character limit for a game name
phrases.usage_guidance: The 12-character figure and 'symbols count double toward it' rule are both already correctly encoded in game-rules.js (ff: limit 12, weighted: true) and match fan-site consensus exactly. IMPORTANT CAVEAT found this pass: this figure could NOT be found anywhere in Garena's own official support article — it is fan-site/community consensus, not first-party-documented. Keep citing it (community consensus is strong and consistent across sources) but don't misattribute it as an official Garena-published number.
phrases.good_example: O limite máximo no Free Fire é de 12 caracteres para o nick completo. [...] Símbolos e espaço invisível também contam.
phrases.avoid_when: citing '12 characters' as an official Garena-documented figure

phrases.english_concept: shareable style template for a whole team/squad
phrases.usage_guidance: This is UTG's own original feature-naming, not an externally-attested phrase — kept as an existing_repo_usage record because it's a strong, natural, well-targeted piece of product copy worth protecting/reusing consistently if the Tag Studio pattern expands to other games (ML, PUBG clan tags per the internal deferred-opportunities list).
phrases.good_example: Você recebe um link que guarda a receita do estilo (fonte + moldura), não um texto pronto. Cada integrante abre o link, digita o próprio nome, e o estilo da tag é aplicado automaticamente
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: accented letters not receiving the stylized variant
phrases.usage_guidance: Existing, accurate, well-framed FAQ answer — keep as-is. This is the BR site's own correct, pre-emptive answer to what independent forum research this pass identified as the actual, better-evidenced 'broken text after paste' pain point (as opposed to the unconfirmed 'texto quebrado'/'bugou o nick' phrasing, which was searched for and not found verbatim anywhere).
phrases.good_example: Os caracteres acentuados (á, é, í, ó, ú, ã, õ, â, ê, ô, ç) costumam ser mantidos como estão na maioria dos estilos [...] Se quiser que todas as letras saiam no mesmo estilo [...] dá pra escrever sem acento
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: block / print capital letters, as taught first in school
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the pt_BR name for the block-letters job. A Brazilian printables page offering unjoined capitals should say 'letra bastão' in the H1 and offer the bastão↔cursiva pairing, because the transition between them ('passagem da letra bastão para a cursiva') is itself a searched parent question.
phrases.good_example: Atividades de letra bastão maiúscula e minúscula para imprimir.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in pt_PT copy — Portugal's school terminology differs and this pass gathered no pt_PT evidence. Do not use it for decorative/Unicode uppercase styling; 'bastão' belongs to the handwriting-teaching register only.

phrases.english_concept: the school stage a sheet is aimed at
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as level labels and as a title qualifier ('… para educação infantil'). 'Alfabetização' is the strongest of the three for printables copy because it names the goal rather than the age, and Brazilian teachers search it as a topic.
phrases.good_example: Atividades de alfabetização com letra bastão e cursiva — 1º ano.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'jardim de infância' (Portugal/older BR usage) or 'pré-escola' as the stage name in current pt_BR copy. Do not translate 'alfabetização' as 'literacy' in bilingual metadata — the register shifts from classroom to policy.

phrases.english_concept: lettering tattoo / tattoo letters (the Brazilian studio-blog head term)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as a secondary/body-copy variant that makes the page sound like it was written by someone inside the Brazilian scene. Keep 'letras para tatuagem' as the H1/slug — that is the fuller search form and is already the live page's target.
phrases.good_example: As duas escolhas devem ser feitas para as letras tattoo: o que escrever e em que estilo escrever.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for pt_PT copy — 'tattoo' as a bare noun in this hybrid is Brazilian scene register; Portugal copy should stay with 'tatuagem'. Do not use it in a formal/editorial FAQ answer where the full Portuguese form reads better.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use when describing the thin-stroke/minimalist style option on the pt tattoo page. Write it as one word to match how Brazilian artists write it — 'fine line' (two words) reads as an English import, 'fineline' reads as scene-native.
phrases.good_example: Faço tatuagens fineline — traço fino, discreto, ideal para nome ou frase curta.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in an accessibility, legal, or technical explanation. Do not use in pt_PT copy without separate evidence. Do not use it as a synonym for 'small' — fineline is about stroke weight, not size.

phrases.english_concept: text-built face emoticon — the everyday Brazilian word
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, category headings, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'carinhas de texto' as the PT head phrase, with 'kaomoji' as the named term (pt.wikipedia has a real Kaomoji article, so the loanword IS established in Portuguese — more so than in Dutch/Polish/Indonesian/Turkish). 'emoticons japoneses' is pt.wikipedia's own stated synonym and works as the meta-description variant.
phrases.good_example: Kaomojis, ou carinhas japonesas, são combinações de caracteres que formam rostos — é só copiar e colar.
phrases.avoid_when: Too soft for competitive gaming-nickname copy (PT-015 'maneiro' / PT-022 aggressive-guild register applies there). Not for technical Unicode copy. Evidence is Brazil-weighted — do not assume it for pt-PT without corroboration.

phrases.usage_guidance: Boundary FAQ only, on ASCII-art and big-text pages. Never product framing.
phrases.good_example: Colar o mesmo desenho várias vezes seguidas é visto como copypasta e costuma render mute na maioria dos servidores de Discord.
phrases.avoid_when: Never in title, H1, meta or CTA; never in printables/education copy.

phrases.english_concept: calligraphy for wedding invitations — the searched Brazilian phrase
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as an FAQ heading only if the answer is honest about what a Unicode tool can and cannot do (it can preview a script look for the names; it cannot replace a hired calligrapher). Do not make it a page target — the SERP is dominated by service providers and studios, not tools.
phrases.good_example: Os convites de casamento podem usar basicamente duas técnicas: a caligrafia feita à mão ou a impressão na gráfica.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Also avoid on any surface where it could imply the site produces printable calligraphy — the site outputs copy-paste Unicode.

phrases.english_concept: wedding stationery — the whole suite of printed pieces
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to name the context a script style is being chosen for. It is background vocabulary that makes copy sound native — not a keyword to target.
phrases.good_example: A fonte escolhida para os nomes costuma se repetir em toda a papelaria do casamento.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Ambiguous in isolation — always qualify it ('papelaria do casamento') or a reader will parse it as 'stationery shop'.

phrases.english_concept: the couple / the couple's names written decoratively
phrases.usage_guidance: Ideal as placeholder/example text in a script-style demo ('Ana & Pedro'), framed as 'os nomes dos noivos'. Supports the page's existing cursive/script target rather than competing with it.
phrases.good_example: Os nomes dos noivos ficam em destaque, e o resto do texto em uma fonte simples.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — 'noivos' in a Free Fire context is nonsense. Also do not use it as a generic word for 'couple': for a dating/romantic-nickname page the site already has PT-021 (apelido carinhoso / nome de casal), which is the right register there.

phrases.english_concept: characters counted with or without spaces
phrases.usage_guidance: Note BR usage tends to singular 'com espaço' in speech; the fetched thread uses both. Use when explaining the with/without-spaces stats.

phrases.english_concept: WhatsApp's "About" / bio field -- the BR-native name for that specific field
phrases.usage_guidance: Already extensively used across live production copy (pt/letras-diferentes/, pt/fontes-para-whatsapp/, pt/category/, pt/library/emoji-combos/) but never had its own phrase_id -- a documentation gap this closes. FINAL-REPORT-2026-07-25.md line 108-111 already names it in passing without a formal row.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not conflate with 'status' (WhatsApp's separate Stories-like feature) or 'nome de contato' (display name) -- all three are distinct WhatsApp surfaces already correctly distinguished in current pt/ copy.

phrases.usage_guidance: A design-history/editorial angle on decorated Portuguese letters — distinct from and uncontested by the gamer-nick-symbol-listicle competitor crowd found in the same research pass.

phrases.native_phrase: Apelidos do Discord / Biografias criativas / Pequenas maiúsculas
phrases.usage_guidance: The only confirmed pt_PT-market source found this pass — pt_PT forum coverage is otherwise near-zero (ZWAME, the flagship pt_PT forum, is blocked). Do not substitute pt_BR slang for pt_PT copy.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not mix with pt_BR gaming slang (e.g. 'Sedex de kill' is Correios-brand-specific and meaningless in Portugal, which uses CTT).
